question.problem:
What is ${\int }_{0}^{2}(x+2)^{3}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?

*Hint: Write down the missing expression in terms of $i$ and $n.$*

${\int }_{0}^{2}(x+2)^{3}\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[($
{{field-1}}
$)^{\,3}\cdot \frac{2}{n}]$
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{i}=a+iΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}(x+2)^{3}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=(x+2)^{3},$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the upper bound is $b=2.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{2-0}{n}=\frac{2}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(x+2)^{3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(0+i\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[f(\frac{2i}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}[{(\,\frac{2i}{n}+2\,)}^{\,3}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
